analysiskit

Turns a 4Mi dataset and a List of Analysis workbook into an MMC-styled results workbook. This package is the analysis itself; the Analysis Kit App is a point-and-click interface on top of it.

Install 

install.packages("pak")
pak::pkg_install("mixedmigrationcentre/analysiskit")

Use 

library(analysiskit)

# 1. Get the List of Analysis template and fill it in
copy_loa_template("resources")

# 2. Check the dataset and the workbook against each other
check_analysis_inputs(
  dataset = "data/my_4mi_export.xlsx",
  loa     = "resources/loa_template.xlsx"
)

# 3. Run, and save the results workbook
run_analysis_locally(
  dataset       = "data/my_4mi_export.xlsx",
  loa           = "resources/loa_template.xlsx",
  output_folder = "output"
)

Step 2 lists anything that must be fixed before a run. Step 3 refuses to start until it is clean, and writes analysiskit_<dataset>_<date-time>.xlsx to the output folder.

The List of Analysis

Write raw question codes (Q27, Q78) everywhere in the workbook. The template’s readme sheet explains each sheet, and the full reference is inst/extdata/loa-schema.md.

analysis_type What you get
prop_select_one % of respondents giving each answer
prop_select_multiple % of respondents selecting each option
mean / median average / median of a numeric question
ratio sum of analysis_var_numerator / sum of analysis_var_denominator

Leave level empty unless a row needs a confidence interval. Rows with a level use the much slower survey engine; the figures are the same either way.

For developers

Every step is also available on its own: read_analysis_dataset(), read_loa_workbook(), build_analysis_spec(), run_analysis_spec(), ak_export_results(). See ?run_analysis_locally and the help pages it links to.

Changes to the analysis are made here, in this package. The app picks them up when the package is reinstalled.
